plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Enormous, ruffled blooms that look like silk pom-poms, often with a rich, sweet perfume. Gardens in the northern temperate zone fill with these flowers as late spring turns to early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Temperate gardens across North America and Europe, and native to northern China and Siberia
plants.funFact: Peonies are long-lived perennials. A healthy plant can keep flowering in the same spot for 50 years or more.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, fragrant mounds send up slender spikes of tiny violet flowers that hum with bees. In early summer the Mediterranean hillsides and the fields of Provence start to turn purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to midsummer (June to August), with blooms opening in June in southern Europe
plants.location: Mediterranean Europe, including Provence, France, and gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin lavare, 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with lavender.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Trees covered in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, which carpet the ground beneath them in violet. In the Southern Hemisphere they are a spectacle of spring, but not in June.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring (October to November) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of the thousands of these trees lining its streets.
